quotes.text: A container isn't a computer, and it doesn't carry its own operating system around. Instead, it borrows the operating system of the machine it's running on, and it packs only the app and the pieces that app depends on.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Explains in one breath what a container is and why it stays small.

quotes.text: When you change something, Docker rebuilds only the layer you changed and the layer sitting on top of it, while everything below stays exactly as it was.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Makes the benefit of image layers concrete for beginners.

quotes.text: A virtual machine buys you stronger separation and pays for it with size and speed. A container buys you speed and a small footprint and pays for it by sharing more with the machine underneath.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: A balanced one-line comparison of containers and virtual machines.

quotes.text: The trouble is that latest changes over time, so the same setup can build differently next month, and pinning a specific version keeps your builds predictable.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: A concrete best-practice recommendation against relying on the latest tag.

quotes.text: Any change you make to a running container disappears the next time you start it, and the image is the source of truth, so the fix belongs there.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: States a key operating principle that prevents a common beginner mistake.

chapters.title: Registries: where images live and travel
Beginner mistakes and when not to use containers

takeaways: A container packages an app with everything it needs and borrows the host operating system, so it runs the same way on a laptop, a server or in the cloud.
Images are read-only, layered blueprints built from a Dockerfile and shared through registries such as Docker Hub, while containers are the disposable running copies.

Containers are smaller and faster than virtual machines, but data belongs in volumes, versions should be pinned instead of using latest, and strong isolation or a different operating system still calls for a virtual machine.
hook: An app that runs perfectly on one laptop and breaks on the next machine costs teams hours of setup and debugging. This episode is for beginners, developers and IT pros who keep hearing about Docker but never got a plain explanation. You will understand containers, images, Dockerfiles, registries and how containers compare to virtual machines, plus the beginner mistakes to avoid.
